topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section sets the lecture aims, introduces the evolutionary progression model of cancer mutations, and frames the discussion around the core hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations alter upstream receptors and intracellular signaling cascades to drive autonomous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations disrupt lineage maturation programs to keep cells trapped in proliferative progenitor states across hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the molecular mechanisms and protein interactions governing the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway and how cancer cells resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore telomere shortening, TERT reactivation mechanisms, and the p53 stress-response pathways that cancer cells circumvent to achieve unlimited replicative potential.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways to support rapid biosynthesis and generate oncogenic metabolites that alter gene expression.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the vascular requirements for sustained tumor growth and the regulatory switch between pro- and anti-angiogenic factors.

topics.label: Metastasis and systemic dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the biological stages, physical and environmental barriers, and genomic features that govern tumor cell invasion and metastatic colonization.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarizes the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks, offers recommended literature, and closes the lecture.
